title: Swing a wheelchair's swing-away footrest out of the way and lift it off its hinge pin
instruction: Swing the wheelchair's blue footrest hanger out to the side, lift it off its hinge pin, and lower it until it rests on the bracket, then let go.
context: Nursing assistants (BLS 31-1131, about 1.3 million US workers) and home health and personal care aides (31-1120, about 3.7 million) swing a wheelchair's footrests out of the way, or lift them off, at nearly every transfer to bed, toilet or car. One hand holds the spring release latch down while the other swings the hanger, because a latch let up early locks the hanger again; the hanger lifts off its pin only once it is swung fully out.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases (bases at x 0, y +-0.305), y to the robot's left, z up; the table top is at z 0.7475. One fixed fixture, a wheelchair front-frame bracket, and one hanger. (1) Bracket: dark grey powder-coated steel, 3.0 kg, bolted to the table: a 200 x 340 x 8 mm base plate (centre x 0.09, y -0.11), a 30 x 30 mm post 100 mm tall at x 0.09, y -0.15, and a 90 x 320 x 10 mm seat plate on top (top face 100 mm above the table, centre x 0.135, y -0.12). (2) Hinge pin: silver steel, 16 mm across, 35 mm tall above the seat plate, at (0.15, -0.15), vertical. (3) Footrest hanger: blue powder-coated steel with an aluminium footplate, 0.80 kg: a 28 mm across x 60 mm tall sleeve on the pin (its bottom 0.5 mm above the seat), a 25 mm across steel tube 288 mm long from the sleeve pointing forward (+x, 0 deg) with its axis 45 mm above the seat, and a flipped-up footplate 4 x 120 x 80 mm at the tube end. Friction 0.8. (4) Release latch: a red pad 28 x 28 x 14 mm on a spring (400 N/m, 3 mm preload, 8 mm travel) at (0.15, -0.02), top face 22 mm above the seat plate. 6 mm of travel frees the pawl; under 3 mm it locks the hanger where it stands. (5) Keeper and stop: the hanger may rise only after it has swung out 85 deg to the right; it rises 35 mm to clear the pin top and rests on the parking stop 40 mm above the seat. No other objects. object_jitter 0.
scoring: Measured every control step from reset in a linkkit History cleared only by the simulator reset (so a swing seen once is never erased): swing = hanger yaw about the pin (0 latched, negative = to the right), lift = sleeve bottom above its seated height, plus the hanger's speed and spin from its pose change between steps and the nearest pad of either gripper to the fixture. Ladder: 0 under 45 deg of swing; 0.25 swung out at least 45 deg at some time; 0.5 at least 85 deg at some time; 0.75 at the end swung 90 +- 5 deg, lifted 38 to 44 mm (clear of the 35 mm pin, on the stop), and still (under 3 mm/s and 3 deg/s) for 1 s; 1.0 also released: every pad point of both grippers at least 30 mm from the fixture and both grippers under 5 mm/s for 1 s (the episode ends once success holds 1 s). Real trial: protractor scale on the bracket for the swing; steel rule from the seat plate to the sleeve bottom for the lift; spring scale on the latch pad (about 4 N to press) with a depth mark at 6 mm; a 30 mm spacer block for the clearance; 60 fps video with a 1 mm scale for stillness (a mark on the footplate moves under 3 mm in the last second).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Set the hanger back on the pin, seated on the seat plate, tube pointing forward (+x); let the latch pad spring up so the pawl locks it. Check the latch pad rests 22 mm above the seat plate and the hanger will not turn with a 5 N push at the footplate.
fidelity: The pin, slide and latch are idealised: the hanger moves on a rigid vertical pin joint plus a slide, the pawl is a stiff brake and the keeper and the 40 mm parking stop are rules applied each control step; sideways travel off the pin is not modelled. Footrest raised to horizontal, footplate flipped up. Steel and aluminium parts are solid colliders at true size and mass.
